name: cocoon
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: transparent 2D game sprite, CLOSED training cocoon for a hand-drawn forest mushroom auto-battler.
Input images: Image 1 is the edit target (existing closed cocoon). Image 2 is a supporting style reference (the recently refined mortar).
Primary request: redraw and improve the closed cocoon with more appealing organic shape and polished, restrained cel shading while preserving its identity. One upright hanging oval cocoon, narrow dark tapered attachment at the top, plump lower end, warm pale khaki/ivory mycelium silk, five broad diagonal overlapping wrap bands. Make the band edges curve around the form, subtle pale folded lips and muted olive shadow wedges suggest layered silk. Keep the silhouette simple, full and readable at 128 pixels.
Style: match the reference game's heavy almost-black slightly hand-inked contours, muted earthy palette, simple broad matte shading. No tiny texture noise; no shine, no glossy streaks, no sparkles, no intricate illustration.
Composition: single front-facing closed cocoon, centered on square canvas, same upright pose and narrow-to-wide proportions as original, entire sprite visible with small transparent safety margin; no stand, ground or cast shadow.
Constraints: opaque colored interior, genuine transparent background with real alpha (not a checkerboard drawing), no extra props, no text, no border. Output one closed cocoon only. Keep all wrapper bands sealed; no opening or face.

name: cocoon_alpha
prompt: Use case: background-extraction. Edit this CLOSED COCOON sprite. The supplied image has an unwanted gray checkerboard painted into the RGB image. Remove the entire checkerboard background cleanly, including its texture and shadows. Keep the cocoon artwork exactly the same. Output an RGBA PNG with a real transparent alpha channel everywhere outside the sprite. Transparency is actual zero-alpha pixels, absolutely not drawn checkerboard squares. Keep the opaque dark outlines and opaque colored silk. Add a small empty transparent margin above the narrow attachment so it does not touch the image edge. One closed cocoon, no extra elements.

name: cocoon_open
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: OPEN empty training cocoon sprite in a 2D mushroom forest game.
Input images: Image 1 is the approved-style CLOSED cocoon and primary identity reference. Image 2 is the old OPEN cocoon, showing the required opening and use.
Primary request: create the OPEN state of exactly the cocoon in image 1. Preserve the same external silhouette, top attachment, overall khaki color, ink outlines, band curves, matte shading and front-facing view. Open a tall vertical organic oval slit in the middle spanning about 60 percent of the body's height and 45 percent of its width, with a dark near-black olive opaque hollow inside. Give the slit a thick warm pale silk inner lip; split band ends subtly curl inward at its sides. It should read as an empty, welcoming training pod, not a cracked egg, peeled banana, torn gore or toothy mouth. Leave the top and bottom intact. No creature inside.
Style: thick almost-black handmade outline, broad simple cel shaded folded silk, earthy ivory/khaki and olive shadows, polished flat game sprite consistent with image 1. No gloss or pinprick highlights.
Composition: one open cocoon centered on square canvas with clear safety margin, entire attachment visible. Same proportions as image 1 so the open and closed states can replace one another without moving.
Constraints: no ground shadow, no props, no text, no sparks. Genuinely transparent background (real alpha), not a painted checkerboard. Opening interior stays opaque dark.

name: arrow
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: bow / crossbow / great-bow shared projectile sprite for a hand-drawn 2D forest mushroom game.
Input images: image 1 is the existing arrow to improve. Image 2 is the current bow, a style and palette reference only.
Primary request: redraw one elegant, clear, right-pointing arrow. Keep the exact horizontal side-view pose, shaft on image horizontal midline, tail on LEFT and tip on RIGHT. A long slim warm muted wooden shaft bordered in almost-black; two forest-teal leaf-shaped fletching fins at the left, with a simple central vein; a compact ivory triangular stone/bone arrowhead on the right with a dark olive-gray shaded facet and one restrained wrap at its socket. Maintain long slim proportions, about six times as long as its maximum fin/arrowhead height. Strong silhouette that reads when only 48 pixels wide.
Style: polished hand-inked cartoon sprite, heavy dark outlines matching image 2, matte flat cel shading, limited muted forest palette. Shaft must remain visible as a continuous straight narrow line. Only broad two-tone shading; avoid microdetail, reflections, shiny streaks.
Composition: single centered horizontal arrow on a square transparent canvas, full arrow uncropped from nock to point, generous empty space above and below; arrow spans about 94% of canvas width but only 15% of canvas height.
Constraints: actual transparent background, not painted checkerboards. No bow, hands, extra arrows, ground, shadow, VFX, text or labels. Preserve right-facing orientation and old arrow length-to-height ratio.

name: spore_bomb_projectile
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: flying SPORE BOMB projectile sprite for a hand-drawn 2D mushroom forest game.
Input images: image 1 is the old projectile, preserving its diagonal oval footprint. Image 2 is its mortar weapon, for palette and drawing style only.
Primary request: improve the plain khaki oval into a compact organic spore pod. Keep one plump oval tilted about 30 degrees upward to the right. Warm pale khaki skin with a muted olive crescent shadow on the lower-right side, three or four broad irregular darker olive spore pores grouped on its upper-left surface, and a couple of gentle curved husk seams. Make it feel like a tough closed puffball seed pod full of spores, immediately readable at about 54 x 43 pixels. Use a substantial near-black outline with naturally irregular but smooth contour, and broad restrained matte cel shading.
Composition: single oval pod centered on a square canvas, preserve the original object's diagonal orientation and oval proportions; object occupies about 60% of canvas width and 48% of height. No detached particles, spore cloud, fuse, explosion, stem, leaves or trailing streaks. No face.
Style: match the mortar's bold cartoon contour and muted forest/ivory palette, opaque interior, simple elegant shape, no shiny white streaks, no fine noise or high-detail illustration.
Constraints: genuine transparent background with real alpha, absolutely no checkerboard drawing, no ground shadow, no backdrop, no text. Output only the projectile.

name: horn_projectile
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: giant horn musical-note projectile sprite for a hand-drawn 2D forest mushroom game.
Input images: image 1 is the existing horn projectile and defines its silhouette: three musical note heads, a connected beamed pair on the left and one flagged note on the right. Image 2 is the horn weapon, a drawing style and palette reference only.
Primary request: polish the musical-note volley into three clean, bold, readable hand-inked musical notes. Preserve the composition: left two notes connected across top by a single beam, the separate right note with a short flag curving to the right, stems upright, oval note heads along the lower edge. Fill their broad faces in warm muted burnt terracotta, with a small deep rust shaded edge; surround with thick almost-black outlines. This should retain the old note cluster's warm coral accent but be more readable against a dark green battlefield than its nearly all-black original. Round the oval heads, unify the stem thickness and generous negative spaces, make the flag taper neatly. Matte broad cel shading, no gloss, no 3D extrusion.
Composition: one compact three-note volley centered horizontally and vertically on a square transparent canvas, entire silhouette contained with about 5% padding on all sides; width about 1.5 times height. Keep left pair and right note separated by a clear empty gap. No staff lines, additional notes, sound rings, sparkles, text or horn object.
Style: consistent with the horn reference's near-black handmade contours and restrained earthy color, graphic clarity at game scale. Actual transparent alpha background, not drawn checkerboard. Opaque colored note interiors; negative spaces fully transparent. No shadow on a background.

name: horn_projectile_clean
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Refine this musical-note projectile for a 2D hand-drawn game.
Image 1 is the edit target. Image 2 is the game's horn weapon style.
Keep the three rust-terracotta musical notes and their arrangement: two beamed notes on the left, one flagged note on the right. Make the right flag ATTACH seamlessly to the top of the right upright stem; it must not float disconnected. Add a crisp thick near-black ink contour around every colored silhouette, same proportionate outline thickness as the horn reference. REMOVE the entire soft black/olive halo, glow and shadows outside the shapes; exterior is fully transparent right up to the clean antialiased contour. Remove 3D extrusion: use flat matte terracotta main fill and just one broad darker rust cel-shaded edge inside the ink outline. Round, compact, friendly hand-inked shapes, no reflective highlights. Preserve warm rust colors and recognizable beamed-pair-plus-single-note identity. Clear gap between the left pair and right single. Clean transparent RGBA PNG; absolutely no checkerboard pixels, background, staff lines, extra symbols or text. Fit the entire note cluster in frame with transparent margins.
